headline: Approved a drainage pipe at 87 Collins Road; Clark Avenue manufacturing building hearing set for November 2.
summary: Neighbors described water running from Collins Road across private driveways and yards. The city's project replaces a 12-inch pipe with a 24-inch pipe to carry stormwater to Coppermine Brook. A two-car garage at 57 Evelyn Road was also approved.
decisions: Approved minutes of the September 2, 2026 regular meeting, 6-0.
Approved minutes of the September 16, 2026 onsite walk, 6-0.
Approved Application #2077 for a two-car garage at 57 Evelyn Road, 6-0.
Declared Applications #2078 and #2079 significant activities and set a public hearing for November 2, 2026, 6-0.
Approved Application #26-467F-319, a floodplain permit for a new drainage pipe at 87 Collins Road, 6-0.
Approved Application #2076, a wetlands permit for a new drainage pipe at 87 Collins Road, 6-0.
Continued the public hearings on the Flex Storage Building at 154 East Main Street to November 2, 2026, 6-0.

a.  Application 2076 — Wetlands application for the installation of a new drainage pipe approximately 
495' ft. in length from Collins Road to a north-west stream at 87 Collins Rd — Lot 51B; Lot 50 —

MOTION: Move to open the Public Hearing for Application #2076— Wetlands application for the installation 
of a new drainage pipe approximately 495' ft. in length from Collins Road to a north-west stream at 
87 Collins Rd — Lot 51B; Lot 50 — Collins Rd & Lot 147 — Stafford Ave; Assessor's Map 53, Lots 
50, 51B, and 147; City of Bristol — Department of Public Works, applicant. 
 
By: Klimek Seconded: Carros
Bristol Inland Wetlands & Watercourses Agency Regular  Meeting of October 5 th , 2026 
of the Conservation Commission of the City of Bristol 
 
 
 
 
– 5 – 
 
 
For: Klimek, Bridges, Massaro, Jarboe, Carros, and R ooks. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The public hearing was opened.  
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., City of Bristol, Department of Public Works, 111 North Main St., representing the 
applicant, Sole purpose of it is to improve the city storm drainage system, as you see before you just going through 
the packet contained within the you know, agenda items.Before you is the area of 87 Collins Road, and if you notice 
that the pink area is the floodway, the top of Mine Brook, the blue area is the area at a hundred year foot floodplain 
for the record. The brown area is the 500-year floodplain, and then you see Collins Road at the front. The purpose of 
this project is really to convey water, stormwater, from Collins Road to the rear of the property to Coppermine Brook. 
It is not going to benefit during a 100-year storm. The real purpose of it is to address the intense driving rains, like 
thunderstorms. The pipe analysis, there's currently a 12-inch diameter pipe. We currently have catch basins. But the 
catch basins a with a 12-inch diameter pipe exceeds the capacity of the pipe, and literally water cascades over onto 
the private property, down the driveway, right through their yard to the copper mine. The sole purpose of the project 
is to increase, go from a 12-inch existing pipe to a 24-inch pipe. There are no permanent impacts to the wetlands, 
impacts would be temporary during construction.  
 
Michelle McKenney, 87 Collins Rd., property owner shared testimony, videos, and photographic evidence of the 
flooding that occurs infront of her house through her driveway and backyard. They frequently have to leave their 
home and drive to St Gregory’s to keep their vehicles out of the waters. She has had issues since 2018. 
 
Eric Madsen, 70 Oak Hill Drive, addressed the commission asked why there is not any consideration best 
management practices that would actually reduce and take the flood water out of the road so it’s not there in the 
first place. Some of those best practices, things that the Conservation Commission could be a resource on, 
permeable driveways, permeable patios, rain barrels, people having rain gardens. Water thirsty plants, plants and 
trees, maybe roadside trees. Swales to contain and absorb the run off. 
 
Mr. Rogozinski stated in respect to best practices, we look at this as a conveyance issue, a conveyance of water from 
Collins Road to the back to Coppermine Brook. From the City’s perspective we have a condition where water from a 
city road is going on to private property, and we take that very seriously in the sense to to mitigate that. So in order 
to mitigate it, we want to increase the conveyance.  The speaker's suggestion that we can go in and, in effect, change 
the characteristics of the entire watershed, by working with property owners, probably over a hundred to get them to 
change their driveways to permeable. Even have them install rain gardens to prevent less water from going to this 
point. The city just simply does not see it as a viable option, and certainly not a viable option in a timely manner to 
help the property owner in question. Once again, we cannot tolerate. I can't as director of public works.  Having 
water from a city road go onto private property, and damage it. I literally have a responsibility to try to prevent that. 
That's why I support and I have moved this project along.
